name: Cloudflare Security Audit Skill
what: An agent skill from Cloudflare that runs a structured security audit of a codebase instead of a one-shot "look for bugs" prompt. It works in phases: map the architecture and keep a coverage ledger, hunt for issues area by area, have a fresh sub-agent try to validate each candidate, write findings as JSON checked against a schema (confirmed, needs validation or rejected), verify each record again, then produce a written report. Cloudflare says it grew out of the internal vulnerability harness described on its blog in June 2026. It is a single skill (security-audit), MIT licensed.
who: Developers and security reviewers who use Claude Code, Codex or another skills-capable agent and want a repeatable audit with evidence for each finding, rather than a list of guesses.

setup.text: Install it into the current project with the open skills CLI (run from the project root). Add --global to install it for your user instead:

Check the requirements first. The README asks for an agent whose model supports tool use and parallel sub-agents, Node.js for the bundled validators, and an OS-enforced sandbox for running any of the target's code. Without the sandbox, leads stay marked as needing validation instead of being confirmed.

Restart your agent so it picks up the skill, then ask for an audit in plain language. Output goes to ~/security-audit-skill/<repo-name>/run-<N> unless you name another folder. Each run writes REPORT.md, FINDINGS-DETAIL.md and NEEDS-VALIDATION.md plus the JSON findings.
Treat the report as a starting point for human review. A full audit uses many sub-agent calls, so it can take a while and use a lot of tokens on a large repository.

prompts: Do a security review of this repo and write the output to ~/audits/my-project.

seo.title: Cloudflare Security Audit Skill: install and use the security-audit agent skill
seo.description: What Cloudflare's security-audit skill does, how to install it with npx skills add, its sandbox and Node.js requirements, and what the report contains.

sections.heading: How an audit runs
bullets: Recon: the agent maps the architecture (architecture.md) and starts a coverage ledger (coverage-ledger.json) so it can track what it has looked at.
Hunting: it works through the code area by area, guided by the ledger.
Validation: each candidate goes to a fresh verifier sub-agent that tries to confirm or reject it.
Structured output: findings are written to findings.json and checked against the bundled report-schema.json, each marked confirmed, needs_validation or rejected.
Verification and reporting: every record is checked again before the Markdown reports are written.

sections.heading: Things to know before you run it
paragraphs: The skill has two modes. Asking it to audit or pen-test a codebase runs the full audit with report files. Security questions and focused work on one issue use a lighter guidance mode unless you ask for the report artifacts.

Validation is only as strong as your sandbox. To execute the target's builds, tests or fixtures, the README asks for an OS-enforced sandbox with no external network, a clean environment, resource limits and writes limited to scratch folders. Without that, candidates stay as needs_validation instead of being run.

faq.a: Any coding agent that supports Agent Skills, with a model that can use tools and run parallel sub-agents. You install it with the open skills CLI, which supports agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode.
Yes. The skill is MIT licensed. You pay only for the model usage of the agent you run it in.
